genre_and_feel: Modern Japanese indie funk-pop and city-pop-adjacent synth-funk with a crisp nu-disco sheen. The feel is bright, stylish, breezy, and effortlessly upbeat—urban and retro-futuristic without sounding heavy, aggressive, or overly sentimental.
tempo_and_groove: Approximately 120 BPM (around 118–122 BPM) in 4/4 time using crisp, straight 16th-note subdivisions (not swung). A steady four-on-the-floor kick drives forward momentum while a tight, dry backbeat locks solidly on beats 2 and 4. Syncopation comes from anticipated 16th-note chord stabs (hitting on the 'e' and 'a' of beats and pushing across barlines on the 'and' of 4), bouncy off-beat bass pickups, and percussive guitar chanks.
drums: A tight, dry acoustic-electronic hybrid kit processed for drum-machine precision. The kick plays a consistent quarter-note four-on-the-floor pulse with rounded, controlled low end and occasional quick 16th-note pickup doubles at phrase turnarounds. The snare delivers a crisp, snappy mid-high crack dead-center on beats 2 and 4 with restrained ghost notes and short, tight fills before choruses. Hi-hats run steady 8th/16th patterns with quick off-beat open-hat barks to lift chorus energy, supported by subtle shaker-like high-end ticks and tightly gated crashes that mark transitions without washing out the pocket.
bass: An active, melodic fingerstyle electric bass with bright round-wound upper-mid clarity and occasional pop-style transient snaps. It anchors the low-to-mid register on downbeats with the kick, then springs upward into middle-register octave leaps, muted 16th-note dead-note ghost pickups, and short staccato phrases that leave rhythmic air. At phrase endings, it steps through brisk diatonic passing runs to propel the harmony into the next bar.
guitars: Clean, glassy single-coil electric guitar (Strat-like bridge/middle quack, lightly compressed and very dry). Its primary role is percussive funk rhythm comping: tight, muted 16th-note strums interspersed with short, clipped chord stabs using upper-register 3- and 4-note voicings on the top strings so it stays well above the bass. Secondarily, it weaves in crisp single-note counter-licks and bright, rhythmic fills in the gaps between vocal or lead phrases.
keys_and_other: A blend of warm electric piano/poly-synth chords for smooth harmonic glue, lush chorus-tinted synth pads during sparser or dreamy breakdowns, and a cheerful, slightly nasal retro bell/square-blend synth lead carrying the main instrumental hook. Subtle digital-nostalgic ear candy—such as soft crystalline synth arpeggios, quick chiptune-adjacent bleeps, and gentle filtered transition sweeps—adds playful polish.
harmony_colour: Bright, lush extended pop harmony influenced by city-pop and light jazz-pop rather than stark rock triads. Relies heavily on major 7ths, minor 7ths, and suspended dominant 9ths/11ths (like V9sus4), colored with occasional secondary dominants and brief modal borrowing from the parallel minor for a warm, wistful tint. Chords turn over briskly—often every 2 to 4 beats—using smooth stepwise root motion, slash-chord inversions, and circle-of-fifths-adjacent turnarounds that keep the progression gliding forward.
melody_style: Conversational, rhythmically agile, and hook-driven. Built from short diatonic and major-pentatonic motifs punctuated by cheerful 5th, 6th, or octave leaps, phrases frequently enter on an off-beat after beat 1 and land cleanly on colorful chord tones (3rds, 7ths, 9ths). It balances tight, rapid-fire staccato rhythmic bursts in verse sections with slightly broader, soaring melodic lines in the chorus, always leaving 1-to-2 beat pockets for guitar or bass responses.
arrangement_build: Dynamic energy shifts rely on muting, space, and layering rather than distortion or loudness jumps. An upbeat instrumental hook states the full pocket immediately; verses strip back slightly so bass, tight drums, and sparse staccato guitar have room to breathe; pre-choruses introduce longer chord holds, rising synth textures, or crisp rhythmic stop-hits to build anticipation; choruses bring in the full dense groove with bright layered synths and open-hat lifts; and a mid-song breakdown drops drums and bass completely into floating, dreamy synth pads before snapping cleanly back into the final chorus.
mix: Ultra-clean, punchy, and modern with a retro-digital sheen. Kick and bass are tightly focused in the low end with zero sub-heavy mud, drums and lead elements sit dry and upfront in the center, and rhythm guitars, electric piano, and pads spread wider in stereo with short, controlled room ambience. Crisp upper-mids give guitar chanks and snare hits tactile snap while airy highs keep synths sparkling without harshness.
why_it_feels_fun: It generates constant forward bounce without heaviness: the four-on-the-floor pulse feels like brisk, cheerful movement rather than urgent stress. Because the bass, guitar, and lead synth all favor short, staccato articulations separated by micro-rests, the arrangement feels light on its feet and uncluttered. Meanwhile, warm major-7th and 9th harmonies soften every turnaround into cozy nostalgia, and playful call-and-response fills between instruments keep repetition engaging.
original_piece_recipe: Set your tempo between 116 and 122 BPM using strict straight 16th-note timing, anchoring the groove with a tight four-on-the-floor kick and a dry, crisp snare on beats 2 and 4.

Compose an original syncopated electric bassline featuring short staccato notes, muted 16th-note ghost pickups, and upbeat octave jumps that lock with the kick on beat 1 while anticipating chord changes on the 'and' of 4.

Track a clean, bright single-coil electric guitar playing clipped 16th-note percussive 'chank' patterns and upper-register 3-note shell voicings, keeping the low-mid frequencies completely clear for the bass.

Write an original chord progression using warm extended harmonies—major 7ths, minor 7ths, and V9sus4 chords—moving smoothly via stepwise bass motion or slash-chord inversions so the loop cycles seamlessly.

Substitute the vocal with a cheerful, upfront instrumental lead (such as a soft retro bell-synth, bright Rhodes melody, or clean guitar hook) playing off-beat motifs that leave 1-to-2 beat pockets for bass or guitar fills to answer.

Keep the drums and bass dry and centered while panning rhythm guitars and electric piano/synth layers wider; avoid distorted tones or long reverb tails so the mix stays crisp underneath café sound effects.

Structure the full loop across an A–B–A'–C arc (around 32 to 48 bars): start spacious in A, add gentle pad swells and a crisp rhythmic pause-hit in B, bloom into full synth-and-hat energy in C, and thin smoothly back to A.

Build a gentle 4-bar atmospheric breather at the end of the cycle—muting the snare or dropping down to warm synth pads and soft bass—to reset the player's ear and prevent fatigue across long café shifts.
